title: Pair Sums to Target
prompt: A checkout system wants to know whether two distinct coupons can exactly match a target discount. Write a function that returns true if any two different array positions add up to the target, otherwise false.

explanation.beginner:
Example: pairSum([2,7,11], 9) produces true. As you visit a value, search for target minus that value among earlier values. Store earlier values so one position is never used twice.

Compare “reports no pair”: input [[1,2,3],7] produces false. Explain which rule causes the difference before writing code.
explanation.junior:
As you visit a value, search for target minus that value among earlier values. Store earlier values so one position is never used twice.

Tempting mistake: Checking after inserting the current item can accidentally pair an item with itself.

Trace the branch conditions and any accumulator or lookup after each input. Keep the return contract separate from how it is calculated. A hash lookup approach has expected O(n) time and O(n) space; checking all pairs costs O(n²).

Regression check: preserve the contract illustrated by “reports no pair”, then change one boundary in a new test. The solution below is one implementation; another is valid when it preserves the same behavior.
